summary: Operator re-anchor surgery 2026-08-10 findings: the 2026-07-22 'chain break at line 78729' is not one incident — breaks recur roughly per cycle from there onward (55 sequential epoch-anchors were needed to green the RUNTIME ledger; the CONSOLE ledger has ~180+ dense breaks and was left at its documented broken state after iterative anchoring proved unsafe — sibling entries SHARE entry_seq values, so `evolve ledger anchor <seq>` can bind an EARLIER line with the same seq and regress the anchor). Cadence + onset (fleet width >1 era) indicate concurrent lane appends interleave prev_hash references: each writer chains onto the tip it read, not the tip at write time. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: (a) serialize append's read-tip->hash->write under the flock sidecar (same pattern as continuation/registry.go WriteRegistryEntry) so prev_hash always names the immediately preceding on-disk line; regression: N concurrent appenders under -race produce a chain that verifies; (b) make `evolve ledger anchor` reject a seq whose line is not the UNIQUE carrier (or take a line SHA directly) so an anchor can never bind backward; (c) add a native `evolve ledger rebaseline` (operator-gated like anchor, ADR-0048-consistent) that seals a densely-damaged prefix in ONE operation — write the in-band operator reset-seal at the tip — instead of requiring hundreds of sequential anchors; then run it on the CONSOLE plane ledger (break at line 78729 onward; .evolve/ledger.jsonl 87k lines) to green it. Evidence: runtime ledger-anchor.json (55th anchor, green); console verify output; tip-mismatch semantics note: verify's 'want' on tip mismatch does NOT come from ledger.tip alone — document the tip-witness resolution while in there.
